title: Inverse image commutes with finite evaluation on ringed sequence sites
statement: Let C and D be sites, F : C → D continuous, and let its product with the identity of the natural-number poset be continuous for the vertical sequence topologies [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site]. Let A and B be ring sheaves on the sequence sites and φ : A → F_* B. Fix n and identify their n-th slices with S and T. Let ψ : S → F_* T be the sliced ring map. Given adjunctions L ⊣ φ_* and L_n ⊣ ψ_* and an isomorphism d : φ_* ev_n ≅ ev_n ψ_*, the inverse mate of d under these two adjunctions is invertible. Thus L commutes with finite evaluation up to the canonical mate isomorphism. All module and ring carriers lie in a universe containing the object and morphism universes of the sites.

source.place: Construction 4.1, finite evaluation of strict varying-ring systems; explicit right-coextension and iterated-mates argument supplied here.

proof.text: Construct a right adjoint to evaluation at n: at (m,U), use the module of functions PLift(n ≤ m) → M(U), with scalars restricted through the horizontal ring map. This gives M(U) for n ≤ m and the zero module otherwise. Restriction uses the vertical restriction of M; the sheaf condition is tested at every vertical slice. The unit is horizontal restriction and the counit evaluates at the reflexive inequality. Check both triangle identities sectionwise.

proof.text: Take the mate of d under the evaluation/coextension adjunctions. At each vertical object, conjugate the bijective section map of d on the coextension at level n by evaluation of functions on PLift(n ≤ n). The mate at level m acts pointwise by this bijection on functions PLift(n ≤ m) → M(FU), since horizontal restriction has identity underlying carrier maps. It is bijective both when n ≤ m and when the function domain is empty. Forgetting to presheaves of abelian groups and reflecting isomorphisms gives invertibility.

proof.text: The iterated-mates identity identifies the preceding mate with the conjugate of the inverse mate under L ⊣ φ_* and L_n ⊣ ψ_*. Conjugation reflects invertibility, proving the assertion.

theorem sequenceModulePullbackEvaluation_isIso
    {D : Type d} [Category.{w} D]
    [UnivLE.{d, r}] [UnivLE.{w, r}] [UnivLE.{max d w, r}]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (K : GrothendieckTopology D)
    (F : C ⥤ D) [F.IsContinuous J K]
    [((𝟭 ℕ).prod F).IsContinuous (coefficientSequenceTopology J)
      (coefficientSequenceTopology K)]
    (A : Sheaf (coefficientSequenceTopology J) RingCat.{r})
    (B : Sheaf (coefficientSequenceTopology K) RingCat.{r}) (n : ℕ)
    (φ : A ⟶ (((𝟭 ℕ).prod F).sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{r}
      (coefficientSequenceTopology J) (coefficientSequenceTopology K)).obj B)
    (S : Sheaf J RingCat.{r}) (T : Sheaf K RingCat.{r})
    (hA : ((Prod.sectR n C).sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{r} J
      (coefficientSequenceTopology J)).obj A = S)
    (hB : ((Prod.sectR n D).sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{r} K
      (coefficientSequenceTopology K)).obj B = T)
    (ψ : S ⟶ (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{r} J K).obj T)
    (L : SheafOfModules.{r} A ⥤ SheafOfModules.{r} B)
    (Ln : SheafOfModules.{r} S ⥤ SheafOfModules.{r} T)
    (adj : L ⊣ SheafOfModules.pushforward φ)
    (adjn : Ln ⊣ SheafOfModules.pushforward ψ)
    (d : SheafOfModules.pushforward.{r} φ ⋙
        SheafOfModules.pushforward (F := Prod.sectR n C) (eqToHom hA.symm) ≅
      SheafOfModules.pushforward (F := Prod.sectR n D) (eqToHom hB.symm) ⋙
        SheafOfModules.pushforward ψ) :
    IsIso ((mateEquiv adj adjn).symm d.hom).natTrans
